q: What do I need to apply to a CBA program as an incoming freshman?
a: Per cpu.edu.ph you need your Senior High School report card, a PSA-authenticated birth certificate, a 2×2 ID picture and, optionally, a certificate of good moral character. If you don't have your final report card yet, a scanned PSA birth certificate and Grade 12 ID are accepted. Requirements can change each school year, so please confirm with the CPU Information Center.

q: Do I need to take the CPU College Aptitude Test (CPUCAT)?
a: According to cpu.edu.ph, CPUCAT is currently required only for Engineering, Pharmacy and Medical Laboratory Science applicants. CBA applicants do not need to take it.

q: How do I start my application?
a: Pre-register online at registration.cpu.edu.ph, pay the ₱500 admission fee through CPU's official payment options, and submit your requirements. After you're admitted, you'll proceed to advising and enrollment at the College of Business and Accountancy.

q: My senior high strand wasn't ABM. Can I still take a BSBA program?
a: Yes. CBA offers Bridging Program curricula for BSBA Business Management and BSBA Financial Management. They add business core courses (Organization and Management, Principles of Marketing, and Business Finance) in your first year so you start on equal footing.

q: Which programs does the College of Business and Accountancy offer?
a: This site covers six programs: BSBA major in Business Management, Financial Management, Marketing Management, and Human Resource Management; BS Entrepreneurship; and BS Management Accounting.
All six programs take four years, with summer terms in the first years. Total credit units range from 140 (most BSBA majors) to 184 (BS Management Accounting).

Yes. Every BSBA major ends with a 600-hour Business Internship. BS Management Accounting has a Management Accounting Internship, and BS Entrepreneurship students implement their own business plan over two semesters.

q: What's the difference between BS Management Accounting and BSBA Financial Management?
a: BS Management Accounting is accounting-heavy: intermediate accounting, cost accounting, auditing principles and taxation, plus management reporting and performance management. BSBA Financial Management focuses on corporate finance, banking, investments, credit and capital markets.

BSBA holds ACSCU-AAI Level IV re-accreditation, valid until December 2028, and CPU is a CHED Center of Excellence in Business Administration. The Department of Accountancy, which offers BS Management Accounting, also holds Level IV status for BS Accountancy.

Each program page shows the current tuition, miscellaneous, laboratory and total fees by year level. Fees may change by school year, so request your official assessment from the CPU Accounting Office or send us an inquiry.
CPU offers academic, athletic, work-student and other grants. Ask the CPU Information Center or our office about current scholarship windows and requirements.

q: What grade do I need to qualify for Latin honors?
a: You must have no grade lower than 2.0, carry the minimum study load, and meet the Honors Point Average bands: Summa cum laude 1.00–1.18, Magna cum laude 1.19–1.37, Cum laude 1.38–1.56. See the Policies page for the full College Honors Policy.

q: What is the passing grade at CPU?
a: The lowest passing grade is 3.0 (C-, 75–76%). Anything below 75% is a 5.0 (F).

q: What student organizations can I join?
a: CBA has the Provincial Board plus ACE, COAP, FIMA, JMA, JMAP, JPAMA, JPIA and ENACTUS. These organizations often compete and win in local, regional and national contests.
On the CPU campus in Jaro, Iloilo City. CBA students also use university facilities like the CPU Gymnasium, swimming pool and track oval.
